verdict.rationale: Honeycomb's docs say traces and logs are stored as structured events that are indexed automatically on every field at ingest and are queryable without a predefined schema. The Query Builder offers WHERE and GROUP BY clauses, so any attribute, including user or request IDs, can be filtered and grouped without defining indexes or pre-aggregating first. missing for 10: an explicit first-party statement about high-cardinality performance or limits, and independent or hands-on corroboration of grouping by fields like user id or request id.

support.subject: As a developer, I can group and filter by high-cardinality fields (user id, request id) without pre-aggregating or defining indexes first

citations.quote: indexed automatically on every field at ingest, and queryable without a predefined schema.
A query in Honeycomb consists of up to six clauses: SELECT... WHERE... GROUP BY... ORDER BY... LIMIT... HAVING
